config.title: Where to Eat Near the Brandenburg Gate - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers on where to eat near the Brandenburg Gate without the tourist-trap prices: the cheap eats, the sit-down escapes, the picnic move, and what changes on a Sunday.

items.q: Where should I eat near the Brandenburg Gate?
items.a: Not on Pariser Platz itself. The square in front of the Gate has only a handful of restaurants and they all charge landmark prices. Walk a few minutes instead: **east toward Friedrichstrasse** for cheap doner, currywurst and bakeries, **west into the Tiergarten** for the Cafe am Neuen See beer garden, or **south to Potsdamer Platz and the Mall of Berlin** for indoor food courts. Everything good is inside a fifteen-minute walk.

items.q: Is there anywhere cheap to eat near the Brandenburg Gate?
items.a: Yes, but you have to walk away from the Gate. Head east toward **Friedrichstrasse**, about ten minutes, and you hit normal streets with **doner and falafel shops, bakeries and Imbiss stands** where a filling lunch is a few euros. A Berlin doner is around six or seven euros and is a meal in itself. The cheapest option of all is a picnic from a bakery or supermarket eaten on the Tiergarten lawns.

items.q: Where can I sit down for lunch near the Brandenburg Gate?
items.a: My favourite sit-down spot is **Cafe am Neuen See**, a lakeside beer garden about a fifteen-minute walk west through the Tiergarten. It serves grilled food, pizza and beer, is open all year, and is a genuine Berlin place rather than a tourist trap. For more choice, walk **south to Potsdamer Platz or the Mall of Berlin**, which have food courts and everyday restaurants aimed at office workers.

items.q: Are the restaurants at the Brandenburg Gate a tourist trap?
items.a: Most of the ones right on and just off Pariser Platz are, yes. The tell-tale signs are **laminated photo menus in several languages, a host waving you in from the street, and "traditional German" dishes at prices no Berliner would pay**. They have no reason to make you happy because you were only ever going to eat there once. Walk on and Berlin gets cheaper and better within a few minutes.

items.q: Where can I eat near the Brandenburg Gate on a Sunday?
items.a: On Sundays the shops, supermarkets and malls close, including the **Mall of Berlin** food court, which catches a lot of visitors out. Restaurants and beer gardens like **Cafe am Neuen See** open normally, so a sit-down lunch is always possible. If you want a picnic, buy supplies at a morning bakery or at the supermarkets **inside Hauptbahnhof or Friedrichstrasse station**, which stay open on Sundays.

items.q: Is there vegetarian or vegan food near the Brandenburg Gate?
items.a: Berlin is one of the best cities in Europe for meat-free food, but almost none of it is at the Gate itself. Walk **ten to fifteen minutes east into Mitte** for dedicated vegetarian and vegan spots, or use the **Potsdamer Platz and Mall of Berlin food courts**, which always have plant-based counters. Even the doner and falafel shops toward Friedrichstrasse do a vegetarian or vegan version, loaded with salad, for a few euros.

items.q: How far is the nearest good food from the Brandenburg Gate?
items.a: Closer than you think. A **two-minute walk west** into the Tiergarten gets you a picnic spot. **Ten minutes east** toward Friedrichstrasse gets you cheap street food. **Ten to fifteen minutes south** at Potsdamer Platz or the Mall of Berlin gets you food courts and restaurants. **Fifteen minutes west** through the park gets you the Cafe am Neuen See beer garden. Nothing worth eating is more than a short stroll away.
